meta.scope: Curated shelf, NOT a census: 3-5 monitors per resolution tier, sized for the job.
meta.price_rule: Every shelf monitor has a price observed at the maker store, Walmart, Best Buy, or Micro Center (Caleb's retailer rule). No Amazon, no Target. Unpriced-at-allowed-source models were cut.
meta.spec_rule: Specs from the manufacturer's own spec table only; marketing-vs-spec conflicts resolved to the spec table and flagged.
meta.size_class_rule: Caleb's bands (set 2026-10-16, correcting the original band): aspect first — 21:9 or wider = 'widescreen' at any inches. Otherwise by size: under 27in = 'small', 27in to 32in = 'office' (the standard office screen is 32in), over 32in = 'large'.
meta.quality_class_rule: premium = OLED, or top published gamut (>=98% DCI-P3) plus a spec'd HDR class. color = published wide gamut (>=95% DCI-P3) or a factory-calibration claim in the spec sheet. sharp = high pixel density for size (>=100 ppi) with IPS-class panel. everyday = standard published panel, nothing more claimed. unspecified = maker published neither gamut nor panel detail (never assumed everyday).

flags: Tilt-only stand in the spec table (no height adjustment); the 100x100 VESA mount is the ergonomic fix.
Speakers are 2Wx2 per the spec table.
